evidence: get_tree_state (file_tree.rs:39) takes &self but acquires RwLock write guards and conditionally reinitializes both self.tree_state and self.current_root — a get_ prefix that hides mutation

process_widget_message (widget_server.rs:193) uses the generic verb 'process' for a function that parses a protocol message and dispatches to typed handlers — 'dispatch_widget_message' or 'route_widget_message' would be more intent-revealing
process_full (agent.rs:476) contrasted with process_with_cancellation — 'full' qualifies the method by what it lacks (no cancel token) rather than what it does; the distinction is implicit
setup_notification_channel (ipc.rs:253) unconditionally returns Ok(None) with a phase-1 comment; the name promises setup/registration but no channel is established
handle_and_emit (filetree/protocol.rs:376) uses an 'and' connector indicating it does two things; the component dispatch pattern in this codebase normally names these separately
handle_key used identically across colony-env-bin, colony-filetree-bin, colony-preview-bin, colony-logs-bin, colony-gitstatus-bin, colony-history-bin — established convention, not a defect
builtin_ prefix on all shell builtin functions is consistent and domain-aligned across the entire builtins.rs module
Abbreviations ctx, cwd, ttl, cmd, buf, idx are used uniformly throughout the codebase with no inconsistencies found
naming_quality.issues_preventing_higher_score: The get_tree_state mutation mismatch is a contract-violating name in an interior-mutability context; process_full vs process_with_cancellation pair creates an asymmetric API surface; setup_notification_channel advertises behavior it does not implement

strengths: Builtin functions in colony-exec/src/builtins.rs use a uniform builtin_ prefix throughout, making the dispatch table at line 226 immediately readable

Panel binary binaries (env-bin, filetree-bin, gitstatus-bin, etc.) share identical handle_key / emit_frame / render_lines conventions — a reader familiar with one binary can immediately navigate all others
Component interface names (id, render, subscriptions, render_block, handle_action) are consistent across PromptComponent and SidebarComponent implementations in colony-ui-core
Common abbreviations ctx, cwd, ttl, cmd are applied uniformly with no inconsistent expansions found
Domain-specific names like invalidate_cache, clear_stale_approvals, rebuild_preserving_expansion, collapse_or_up communicate intent at the right level of abstraction
naming_quality.issue_character: Naming defects are concentrated at boundary functions where a name promises one kind of behavior (pure read, initialization, setup) but the implementation does another; generic verbs (process) appear at integration seams rather than in domain-core code.
naming_quality.score_rationale: The codebase scores above average for naming: domain-core functions have precise, intent-revealing names and conventions are consistent within each subsystem. The score is held back by a small cluster of boundary-function misnomers (get_ that mutates, process_ that dispatches, setup_ that does nothing) and one asymmetric API pair (process_full vs process_with_cancellation) that forces callers to understand the distinction from context rather than from the names themselves. These are module-scoped issues rather than systemic codebase-wide failures, placing the score in the upper-middle range.

issues.summary: get_tree_state mutates internal state via RwLock writes behind a get_ prefix
evidence: fn get_tree_state(&self, root: &Path) -> Option<TreeState> acquires self.current_root.write() and self.tree_state.write() and conditionally overwrites both (lines 40-58)
Rust convention: get_ methods are expected to be read-only accessors; callers of &self methods do not expect mutation
issues.suggestion: Rename to ensure_tree_state or load_or_init_tree_state to signal that it may initialize on first call or when the root changes

issues.summary: setup_notification_channel always returns Ok(None) — name promises initialization that never happens
evidence: fn setup_notification_channel(_config: &IpcConfig) -> Result<Option<IpcSender<TupleNotification>>> { Ok(None) } with comment 'For phase 1: Just create a channel but don't connect yet' (lines 253-259)
The name 'setup' implies the channel is created/registered; callers cannot distinguish 'disabled by config' from 'not yet implemented'
issues.suggestion: Either rename to placeholder_notification_channel or, better, inline the phase-1 stub at the call site in IpcTupleSpace::open with a TODO comment so the unused function does not mislead future readers

issues.summary: process_full / process_with_cancellation pair uses 'full' as a negative qualifier rather than describing what the method does
evidence: pub async fn process_with_cancellation(...) at line 359 is the primary method with explicit cancel token
pub async fn process_full(...) at line 476 handles the streaming/tool-call path — 'full' contrasts with 'with_cancellation' but does not describe the streaming behavior
A reader must read both bodies to understand that process_full is the streaming tool-use path
issues.suggestion: Rename process_full to run_turn or execute_turn to name what it does, and consider whether process_with_cancellation should be the primary public API; the current naming makes the streaming path look like an enhanced version rather than a distinct code path

issues.summary: process_widget_message uses generic 'process' verb at a dispatch boundary
evidence: async fn process_widget_message(json: &str, ...) -> Option<String> at line 193 parses JSON, matches on ProtocolMessage variants, and routes to typed handlers
The function is purely a dispatcher — callers already know a message is being processed; the name adds no information about what happens to the message
issues.suggestion: Rename to dispatch_widget_message or route_widget_request to communicate the routing/dispatch nature of the function

root_causes: Boundary and integration-seam functions (IPC, widget protocol, tree state initialization) received less naming attention than domain-core functions where the domain vocabulary is clearer
The get_ prefix convention is violated in one interior-mutability context where the borrow checker accepts &self but mutation still occurs through Arc<RwLock<_>>
likely_symptoms: NQ-03 may be symptom-level: process_full vs process_with_cancellation asymmetry may reflect an incomplete refactor rather than a naming decision
possible_false_positives: handle_key across panel binaries — flagged by mechanical scan but is a well-established codebase convention used identically in 6+ binaries
on_event in manager/subscription/renderer — generic observer name but used consistently as a cache-invalidation notification across all three sites
